summary: Staging Private env: Grafana provisioning fails (403 RBAC) during Private observability min pack install
environment: staging (private-stg-lab-usw2) / Kubernetes v1.28 / customer-managed Grafana (in-cluster) + Prometheus Operator
description:
Issue summary
Grafana provisioning (dashboards + datasources) fails in staging Private environment during installation of the Private Observability Minimum Pack. Provisioning job/pod receives 403 Forbidden from the Kubernetes API when attempting to create/update ConfigMaps and Secrets used for Grafana provisioning.

Impact
- Blocks staging validation of the Private observability min pack (dashboards don’t appear in Grafana, datasources not configured).
- Blocks Solutions from running go-live checklist and demoing “day 1 usable” dashboards.
- Causes confusion because install completes with partial success; operator only notices missing dashboards later.

What we expected
Installer/helm chart should provision Grafana objects (ConfigMaps/Secrets) in the target namespace when provisioning is enabled, with least-privilege RBAC that works out of the box.

What happened
Provisioning pod fails with RBAC error:
- Forbidden: cannot create/update configmaps/secrets in namespace
- Forbidden: cannot list/watch configmaps for folder provisioning

Environment details
- Cluster: private-stg-lab-usw2
- Namespace: redwood-private
- Grafana deployed via redwood-helm-charts (grafana enabled)
- Auth: internal-only (no external IdP), default service accounts

Steps to reproduce
1) Deploy Private stack via installer with observability pack enabled:
   - redwood-private install --values values-staging.yaml --enable-observability-pack
2) Grafana comes up, but “Redwood Private / Min Pack” folder is missing.
3) Check provisioning pod/job logs:
   - kubectl -n redwood-private logs job/grafana-provisioner

Relevant logs (trimmed)
E0211 10:42:13.882 provisioning: failed applying dashboard ConfigMap: configmaps is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:redwood-private:grafana-provisioner" cannot create resource "configmaps" in API group "" in the namespace "redwood-private"
E0211 10:42:13.883 provisioning: failed applying datasource Secret: secrets is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:redwood-private:grafana-provisioner" cannot create resource "secrets" in API group "" in the namespace "redwood-private"
E0211 10:42:13.884 provisioning: failed listing existing dashboards: configmaps is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:redwood-private:grafana-provisioner" cannot list resource "configmaps" in API group "" in the namespace "redwood-private"

Notes / hypotheses
- Helm chart creates the grafana-provisioner ServiceAccount but Role/RoleBinding is either missing or not applied when grafana provisioning is enabled.
- In this environment, PSP/OPA is not enforced; this appears to be a plain RBAC gap.

Request
1) Fix chart/installer RBAC defaults so provisioning works in a standard install.
2) Document minimum required RBAC + how to run provisioning in customer-managed Grafana scenarios.
3) Add installer post-install validation to fail loudly when provisioning is enabled but RBAC prevents applying objects.
comments: 2025-02-11 09:18 Markus Klein (Reporter): Hit this in private-stg-lab-usw2 while validating the min pack. Grafana is reachable, but no dashboards/folder show up. Provisioner job logs show 403 forbidden for configmaps/secrets. This blocks our internal runthrough for next week’s customer PoC. Can we patch RBAC + add docs on the required role bindings?

2025-02-11 11:02 Bruno Silva (Assignee): Acknowledged. Reproduced in staging with the same values file. The ServiceAccount exists (grafana-provisioner) but there is no Role/RoleBinding granting create/update on configmaps/secrets in namespace redwood-private. Investigating chart templates + installer wiring.

2025-02-12 10:26 Sergio Costa: The observability-pack provisioning framework assumes the installer/helm layer can apply ConfigMaps/Secrets into the Grafana namespace. We should keep least-privilege but it still needs create/update/list/watch for configmaps + get/create/update for secrets (datasource creds). No cluster-wide perms required.

2025-02-12 14:45 Marcus Lin: Please ensure RBAC is namespace-scoped only. Avoid broad permissions (no '*' verbs, no clusterrole unless absolutely necessary). Also ensure the provisioning Secret does not contain long-lived admin credentials; prefer token with limited scope or K8s-side provisioning.

2025-02-13 16:10 Bruno Silva: Proposed fix drafted: add a namespaced Role + RoleBinding for grafana-provisioner SA gated behind grafana.provisioning.enabled=true, with verbs limited to get/list/watch/create/update/patch on configmaps and get/create/update/patch on secrets. Also adds explicit note in values.yaml to change namespace if Grafana is deployed elsewhere. Pushing PR to redwood-helm-charts.

2025-02-14 09:05 Bruno Silva: PR opened: redwood-helm-charts/pr-512 adds Role/RoleBinding + clarifies SA naming. Also updated installer step to surface provisioning failure as a hard error when enabled (in redwood-private-installer wiring).

2025-02-17 13:22 Sahana Iyer: Validated on staging after applying chart from PR-512: provisioning job succeeds, dashboards folder appears, datasource configured, no extra cluster-scoped RBAC created. Confirmed promtool checks are unaffected. Suggest we also add an installer validation check for RBAC (kubectl auth can-i) before running provisioning.

2025-02-18 10:41 Markus Klein: Re-tested end-to-end with latest staging bundle. Dashboards now present on first install; no manual kubectl rolebinding needed. Please make sure docs include the “customer-managed Grafana in different namespace” setup and troubleshooting section for 403 errors.
resolution:
Resolved via RBAC additions in redwood-helm-charts to grant the grafana-provisioner ServiceAccount namespace-scoped permissions required to apply Grafana provisioning ConfigMaps/Secrets when provisioning is enabled, plus installer-side surfacing of provisioning failures.

Resolution details
- Added Role/RoleBinding for grafana-provisioner SA (namespace-scoped, least-privilege).
- Verified in staging that provisioning job completes and dashboards/datasources are present.
- Action for Docs (tracked in ENG-2848): add explicit troubleshooting steps for 403 RBAC errors and document how to set provisioning namespace/serviceAccount when Grafana is customer-managed.

Workaround (prior to fix)
Manually create a Role + RoleBinding granting the provisioning SA create/update/list/watch on configmaps and create/update on secrets in the Grafana namespace, then re-run the provisioning job.

Follow-ups
- Add a preflight `kubectl auth can-i` check in installer validation (recommended under ENG-2852 post-install report).
